traits.label: Hymenium
traits.text: Gills that are white to cream, adnate to emarginate, not particularly crowded.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium: Gills that are white to cream, adnate to emarginate, not particularly crowded.

traits.label: Cap
traits.text: 4-8 cm in diameter. Convex becoming broadly convex to nearly flat in age, dry and slightly scaly, colors ranging from yellow-brown to reddish-brown.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Cap: 4-8 cm in diameter. Convex becoming broadly convex to nearly flat in age, dry and slightly scaly, colors ranging from yellow-brown to reddish-brown.

traits.label: Hymenium Attachment
traits.text: Adnate to emarginate.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Adnate to emarginate.

traits.label: Stipe
traits.text: Cylindrical, firm, usually lighter at the top and darkening towards the base, often with white to off-white fibrils.
traits.raw: ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, firm, usually lighter at the top and darkening towards the base, often with white to off-white fibrils.

traits.label: Fruit body
traits.text: 5-12 cm tall.
traits.raw: 📏 5-12 cm tall.

traits.label: Spore print
traits.text: Spore Print: White.
traits.raw: ⚪ Spore Print: White.

traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Mycorrhizal, growing exclusively under birch in deciduous and mixed forests.
traits.raw: 🌳 Mycorrhizal, growing exclusively under birch in deciduous and mixed forests.

traits.label: Edibility
traits.text: Edible, but not highly regarded. Some caution advised as it can be confused with toxic species.
traits.raw: 😑 Edible, but not highly regarded. Some caution advised as it can be confused with toxic species.

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: 5-8 x 3-5 µm, elliptical, hyaline.
traits.raw: 🔬 5-8 x 3-5 µm, elliptical, hyaline.

traits.label: Odour
traits.text: Mild to somewhat mealy.
traits.raw: 👃 Mild to somewhat mealy.

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Recognized by its yellow-brown to reddish-brown cap and its presence in both deciduous and coniferous woodlands. The adnate to emarginate gill attachment and the white spore print are also indicators.
traits.raw: 🔤 Recognized by its yellow-brown to reddish-brown cap and its presence in both deciduous and coniferous woodlands. The adnate to emarginate gill attachment and the white spore print are also indicators.

observations.caption:
👇 ...
🆔 Tricholoma fulvum (DC.) Bigeard & H.Guill.
🌐 https://www.gbif.org/species/5241793
📖 (1909). Fl. Champ. Supér. France (Chalon-Sur-Saône) 1: 89.
🇺🇸 Birch Knight
🇩🇪 Gelbblättriger Ritterling
🇪🇪 Kollakaspruun heinik
🇷🇺 Рядовка жёлто-бурая

🗓️ 02/Sep/23, 3:16 PM
🌎 Jaapani Aed, Kadriorg, Tallinn, Harju County
🌳🛣️ Urban park zone with birch (Betula spp.) plantations
🍄 Tricholomataceae / Agaricomycetes

ℹ️ Hymenium: Gills that are white to cream, adnate to emarginate, not particularly crowded.
ℹ️ Cap: 4-8 cm in diameter. Convex becoming broadly convex to nearly flat in age, dry and slightly scaly, colors ranging from yellow-brown to reddish-brown.
ℹ️ Hymenium Attachment: Adnate to emarginate.
ℹ️ Stipe: Cylindrical, firm, usually lighter at the top and darkening towards the base, often with white to off-white fibrils.
📏 5-12 cm tall.
⚪ Spore Print: White.
🌳 Mycorrhizal, growing exclusively under birch in deciduous and mixed forests.
😑 Edible, but not highly regarded. Some caution advised as it can be confused with toxic species.
🔬 5-8 x 3-5 µm, elliptical, hyaline.
👃 Mild to somewhat mealy.
🔤 Recognized by its yellow-brown to reddish-brown cap and its presence in both deciduous and coniferous woodlands. The adnate to emarginate gill attachment and the white spore print are also indicators.

🎞️ MF, ISO 6400, 1/200s, ƒ/11, 0 ev
🔆 Overcast with some rain

🖼️ no crop, 3:2
📌 59°26'30.9"N 24°47'52.5"E
🔦 no flash

📷 Sony α7 III (ILCE-7M3)
🔭 Sony FE 90mm F2.8 Macro G OSS (SEL90M28G)
👋 Handheld, manual mode
🔎 90mm (35mm), 90mm
